scope: Czech/Hungarian Korean-course unique 500–999, 500 entries per locale.
status: authoring complete; independent language/teacher review required; source issues pending
validation: All 5586 entries passed exact range/schema/source SHA256, nonempty strings, ordered Hangul/Jamo sequence, numeric token multisets, blanks/placeholders, equation/arrow signatures and protected excerpts. Preserved targets match source exactly. Native international taxi is intentionally identical with localized role. Earlier context-recorded romanization spans rechecked in both locales; all preserved. These are structural checks, not semantic approval.
method: Native Czech/Hungarian phrase and meaning authoring, reused across identical instruction/meaning patterns; Korean syllables, target strings, romanization and intentional wrong Korean options retained. No external translation API. Original Korean/canonical contexts used to resolve compressed English glosses. Existing RO/FI issue reports used as issue evidence, not as translation text or approval.

contextPolicy.existingGender: unspecified unless explicit in the same source; no gender inferred from Minsu, Mina, Kim, Park, Lee or occupations
contextPolicy.number: Explicit numbers preserved; unspecified human counts remain unspecified in internal interpretation. Hungarian impersonal plural reporting and Czech generic singular role nouns do not establish new semantic participant counts.
contextPolicy.subjectObject: Reporter, embedded friend/weather/rain, addressee and causative younger-sibling objects kept distinct. Unknown omitted subjects remain unknown.
contextPolicy.grammaticalGender: Czech generic masculine role nouns přítel, žák, lékař, sourozenec are grammatical choices, not authored male settings. Impersonal/present constructions preferred where practical. Hungarian does not assign grammatical person gender.
contextPolicy.explicitGender: Woman-speaker older-brother/older-sister definitions 203/204/999/1000/1001/1003 and lexical father/mother/grandmother meanings remain source-explicit.
contextPolicy.courseStages: K1–K10 are course stages, not official proficiency grades.

issues.reason: English equates a whole counting sequence with only the missing two/eight/three. Canonical accepted blank answer establishes the intended word. Native gloss explicitly attributes that meaning to the missing word within the unchanged complete sequence; original source issue remains recorded.

limits: Independent AI review, native-speaker review, Korean phonetics review, teacher review and learner runtime testing have not been completed. No shared source/application files, registry, deployment, commits or pushes changed.
